cim: Miss Universe 2026 Faces Backlash for Response to AI Question
cim_eredeti: Miss Universe 2026 Faces Backlash for Response to AI Question
szoveg_eredeti:
Barreto was asked by the judging panel, “As artificial intelligence grows, what is the most important human value we should never lose?”

Tabitha Parent is a writer at PEOPLE covering entertainment and culture. She joined PEOPLE in 2024. Her work has previously appeared in Marin Magazine, 57 & 65° Magazines and The San Francisco Bay Times.

Miss Universe 2026 Jennifer Barreto is facing criticism for her response to a question about AI during the pageant’s final moments. After being named among the top five finalists during last night’s pageant competition, Barreto and her fellow finalists (Miss Universe New Zealand Georgia Waddingham, Miss Universe Dominican Republic Melissa Núñez, Miss Universe Philippines Bea Millan-Windorski and Miss Universe Venezuela Clara Vegas) were each asked different questions live as part of the final judging process. Barreto, who ultimately took home this year’s crown, was asked by one of the randomly selected judges about her thoughts on artificial intelligence. Particularly, she was asked, “As artificial intelligence grows, what is the most important human value we should never lose?”

Barreto gave her reply in Spanish with an interpreter translating her words, saying, “Artificial intelligence came here to stay, and I think the most important thing is to use it carefully. And then if Artificial Intelligence could replace our values, then it was never a value. Value is what made us, us, and stay true to ourselves.”While Barreto’s answer was met with raucous applause from the audience in her home territory of Puerto Rico, people online seemed to react differently.Many compared Barreto’s answer to a chatbot, leaving comments on the official Miss Universe Instagram page. One commenter wrote, “MISS CLAUDE 🗣️” while another wrote, “Miss chat GPT” and another added, “Miss Gemini,” referring to different AI chatbot models available right now.Others pointed out that the time limit on contestants’ answers appeared to apply loosely to each contestant: “I honestly don’t see the purpose of having a 30-second time limit if the microphone doesn’t automatically shut off once the time is up.”

“The rules should be fair and consistent for all candidates, without allowing anyone extra time to complete their answers. In Puerto Rico’s case, during the final question, the host asked the question in English, but her interpreter translated it into Spanish before she answered in English. Regardless, her answer still sounded rehearsed. #justsaying.”Barreto, 27, made history at last night’s Miss Universe competition, which was hosted in Puerto Rico, becoming the first mother and married woman to take home the crown. Barreto, who is a psychologist and social worker, has a 7-year-old daughter named Penelope.

Miss Universe 2025 Fátima Bosch crowned her successor, bestowing the organization’s newest crown, designed in collaboration with designer George Wittels and Maison d’OR, called “The Radiance of an Eternal Legacy,” which features 3,150 diamonds set in 18-karat white gold.

Competitors came from more than 110 other countries and territories, including a few that had never participated in the final before, such as Miss Universe Saint Martin and Miss Universe Uganda. TV show host Mario Lopez and Miss Universe 2022 R’Bonney Gabriel hosted the fête. According to the hosts, this year’s cast of 117 delegates was made up of 22 contestants with master’s degrees, five doctors and 10 mothers.
